chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who intended to have unlawful intercourse with a woman, so she threw a rock at him and it struck him and killed him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon her regarding what is between her and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and if she is brought to a just Imam, he would stave off his blood (wergild).'

key_terms.إِهْرَاقُ الدَّمِ: Staving off blood money / Waiving the diyya
key_terms.حَرَاماً: Unlawful (specifically referring to unlawful sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a woman who kills a man who attempted to rape her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudence of 'killing for a specific cause' (qatl li-ll-sabab), establishing that if a woman kills a man who forcibly attempted unlawful intercourse with her, she is exempt from paying diyya (blood money) to the victim's heirs. While the Imam holds the discretion to enforce this judicially, the ruling emphasizes her complete exoneration from financial liability, reflecting the Shia principle that the aggressor's fault absolves the defender of compensation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, both together from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who intended upon a woman unlawfully, so she pelts him with a rock, and he is hit from it and is killed. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon her regarding what is between her and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and if she is brought to a just Imam<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> would stave off his blood (wergild)’.
